facts.text: USMU is the Python interface for the USB SMU device over a virtual COM port (VCP)
The constructor opens a pyserial Serial connection on the given port and baud rate and resets its input and output buffers
enable_output writes 'CH1:ENA'; disable_output writes 'CH1:DIS' and documents the disabled state as high impedance
set_current_limit writes 'CH1:CUR <current_mA>', the sink/source current limit in mA
set_voltage writes 'CH1:VOL <voltage_V>', the output voltage in volts
set_voltage_and_measure queries 'CH1:MEA:VOL <voltage_V>' and parses a comma-separated voltage,current reply
set_oversample_rate writes 'CH1:OSR <oversample>'; the docstring states a default of 25, not a permitted range
read_adc queries 'ADC <adc_channel>', a differential conversion between adjacent ADC channels (0 = 0+1, 2 = 2+3), and returns a signed int16 value
lock_current_range accepts only 1, 2, 3 or 4 and writes 'CH1:RANGE <range_val>'
close closes the serial connection if it is open
The README says output voltage, current limit, oversampling rate, DAC values and other settings are settable and that voltage and current are measured in a single command
The README uses a 20 mA current limit and a 1 V setpoint as usage examples; it states no bound

measures.description: Identification string returned by the *IDN? query
measures.name: identification

measures.description: Signed 16-bit differential ADC conversion between channels 0 and 1 (the upstream 'ADC 0')
measures.name: adc_0_1
